text:
Jake Guentzel turned two goals against Washington on Nov. 17 into an NHL.com headline and a spot sixth on the league's goal list, per CBS Sports. Thirteen goals in 23 games, 28 points, 14 points in his last ten: at 32, the Stanley Cup winner from Pittsburgh's 2017 run is giving Tampa Bay exactly what it pays him for, and then some.

Some of that "and then some" is borrowed. He has 13 goals on 9.6 expected (expected goals measure the quality of his chances), shooting 21% after 17% last season, and the Lightning have scored 8.8 more goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice. The underlying work is excellent, though: Tampa takes nearly 62% of the expected goals at five on five when he plays, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking has him living in the home-plate area in front of the net. Evolving-Hockey does warn that his linemates rank in the 90th percentile, which flatters anyone. Our numbers still see a 33 to 49 goal season. You'd expect the finishing to drift back toward normal; the chances are the part worth believing.
headline: Guentzel is scoring like a man possessed
